field_dimensions.previous_assumption: Used 53.3 yard width (NFL standard) and 100 yard length
field_dimensions.correction: Must recalibrate all field projections to 80x40. Formation spread calculations were based on wrong field width.
field_dimensions.impact: Medium - affects formation classification thresholds and field zone labels

first_downs.rule: First downs are by crossing 20-yard ZONE LINES, NOT by gaining 10 yards
first_downs.correction: First down zones are every 20 yards. The field has 4 zones. This changes down-and-distance analysis significantly.
first_downs.impact: High - 20-yard zones means drives need bigger chunks. 4th down decisions are different.

scoring.rule: TD=6, then choose: 1pt from 5yd, 2pt from 10yd, 3pt from 20yd
scoring.game1_note: Final score 14-7. Gators: 2 TDs (1 pick six + 1 offensive). If both went for 1pt XP from 5yd = 14. Tennessee: 1 TD + 1pt XP = 7. Score checks out.
scoring.flag: Need to confirm: did both Gators TDs include successful extra points? 6+1+6+1=14. Tennessee 6+1=7.

defensive_line.rule: Defense must line up 5 yards off the ball
defensive_line.impact: This explains why we see Cover 2 so often - with 5 yards of cushion, the defense naturally sets up with depth. This is NOT the same as NFL/college where the DL is on the ball.
defensive_line.analysis_note: Blitz detection needs recalibration - a 'blitz' in WCFL means a player crosses the 5-yard cushion at the snap, not rushing from the LOS.

punt_rule.rule: Declared punt = ball moved 30 yards from LOS. No actual kick.
punt_rule.game1_note: Gators punted once. Ball would have moved 30 yards from wherever they were.
punt_rule.analysis_note: Punt is a strategic field position decision. Inside opponent's 40 = only half the distance.

fumbles.rule: Ball is DEAD when it touches the ground. No fumble recoveries.
fumbles.impact: This means turnovers are ONLY: interceptions, turnovers on downs, or illegal plays. No fumble chaos.

must_play_rule.rule: All players must play half the game. Each half: on offense OR defense for the entire half. Sideline clears on every change of possession.
must_play_rule.impact: HIGH - this is a major compliance rule. Our playing time tracker should flag any player not getting half the game. Also means players swap offense/defense at halftime, not during.
must_play_rule.compliance_check: Need to verify from tracking data: are all 7+ players getting roughly equal time? Is anyone being left out?

screening.rule: Offensive player cannot impede rusher in ANY way. Rusher has right to clear path to QB.
screening.note: This is different from traditional blocking. There is NO blocking in this league. The only exception is a stationary player.
screening.analysis_note: Any pre-snap motion that puts a player in the rusher's path could be a screening penalty if they don't stop before the snap.

4th_down_context.note: With 20-yard first down zones, 4th down comes up more often and requires bigger gains to convert. The 2 turnovers on downs make more sense in this context - they may have needed 8-12 yards, not 2-3.
4th_down_context.recommendation: When facing 4th and long (10+ yards to the zone), the punt (30 free yards) may be the better play. Save 4th down attempts for 4th and short.

extra_point_strategy.note: Going for 2 (from 10yd) or 3 (from 20yd) is a significant strategic decision. A 3-point conversion from 20 yards is very hard but game-changing.
extra_point_strategy.recommendation: In a close game, the 1-point from 5 yards is safe. But if trailing, the 2-point from 10 gives better expected value than 3-point from 20.

onside_conversion.note: If trailing by 9 or fewer with under 2 min, you can attempt an onside conversion from your own 20 (must cross the 40). This is a 20-yard play.
onside_conversion.recommendation: Have a specific onside conversion play ready. If you're down 7 and score with 1:30 left, you NEED this play.
